history.heading: Mountain nomads
paragraphs: Kyrgyzstan is a mountainous country in Central Asia, dominated by the Tian Shan range. The Kyrgyz people's ancestors lived in the Yenisei region of Siberia and migrated to the area over centuries. Silk Road routes crossed the region, and Sulaiman-Too mountain in Osh was a sacred site.

The region was ruled by various Turkic and Mongol powers and later the Kokand Khanate. The Russian Empire annexed it in the 1870s. A 1916 revolt against conscription was brutally suppressed, and many Kyrgyz fled to China.

history.heading: Soviet era and independence
paragraphs: Under Soviet rule, the Kyrgyz SSR was created in 1936, and the nomadic population was forced into collective farms. Kyrgyzstan became independent on 31 August 1991.

It was initially seen as the most democratic Central Asian state, but presidents were overthrown in popular uprisings in 2005 (the Tulip Revolution), 2010 and 2020. Ethnic clashes between Kyrgyz and Uzbeks in Osh in 2010 killed hundreds. Sadyr Japarov came to power in 2020 and has concentrated authority. Border clashes with Tajikistan occurred in 2021 and 2022, followed by a border agreement in 2025.

culture.heading: Nomadic traditions
paragraphs: Kyrgyz and Russian are official languages. Most people are Sunni Muslim. The Epic of Manas, one of the longest epic poems in the world, is recited by storytellers called manaschi and is central to national identity.

Traditional culture includes yurts, felt carpets (shyrdak), horse games such as kok-boru and eagle hunting. The World Nomad Games have been held in Kyrgyzstan. Beshbarmak and kumys are traditional food and drink. Issyk-Kul is one of the largest mountain lakes in the world.

politics.heading: Presidential system
paragraphs: Since a 2021 constitutional referendum, Kyrgyzstan has had a strong presidential system. Critics say press freedom and civil society have been increasingly restricted, with journalists and opposition figures arrested.
Kyrgyzstan is a member of the Eurasian Economic Union and the CSTO, hosts a Russian air base, and has deep economic ties with China.

economy.heading: Gold and remittances
paragraphs: Kyrgyzstan is one of the poorer countries in Central Asia. Gold, especially from the Kumtor mine, is the main export. Remittances from migrants working in Russia make up a very large share of GDP. Agriculture and livestock are important, and tourism is growing.
Re-export trade to Russia has increased since 2022, drawing scrutiny over sanctions. The currency is the som.
